## Appearance

Priscilla is described as pale, fair, and spiritual-looking, with a golden and fair appearance when dressed in silk attire. Her husband raved over her ethereal, golden beauty.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c20 P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022), [v4 c1 P24](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0024)_

## Personality

While appearing pale and spiritual, Priscilla is thoughtful, imaginative, and ambitious. She is full of mischief, pranks, and fun. She enjoys joking with friends and teasing others to their faces.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v3 c6 P12](../source/v03-c06.md#nw-v03-c06-p0012)_

## History

Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy, where she formed a close circle of friends with Anne Shirley and Stella Maynard. She later taught school in Carmody before taking her own home school. While on the Island, she presented a paper on cemeteries to the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and brought her aunt, the famous writer Mrs. Charlotte E. Morgan, to visit Anne at Green Gables. Priscilla went on to attend Redmond College in Kingsport, living as housemates with Anne Shirley, Philippa Gordon, Stella Maynard, and Aunt Jamesina at Patty's Place. In her senior year at Redmond, she focused her studies on classics. Following college, she married a handsome foreign missionary and relocated to Japan.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P4](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0004), [v2 c1 P57](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0057), [v2 c15 P23](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0023), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c20 P22](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0022), [v2 c20 P23](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0023), [v3 c1 P21](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0021), [v3 c10 P52](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0052), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c35 P28](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0028), [v4 c1 P22](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0022), [v4 c1 P24](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0024), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Quotes

> I would wish to be famous  <sub>[v2 c13 P34](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0034)</sub>

> Is that Gilbert Blythe over there, Anne? How he has grown up this past year! He was only a schoolboy when I taught in Carmody. And of course that’s Charlie Sloane. He hasn’t changed—couldn’t! He looked just like that when he was born, and he’ll look like that when he’s eighty. This way, dear. We’ll be home in twenty minutes.  <sub>[v3 c3 P15](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0015)</sub>

> And we’re from the Island  <sub>[v3 c4 P31](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0031)</sub>

> I suppose they’ll take them off when they really begin to trot, but I know they’ll take their knitting with them everywhere. They simply couldn’t be parted from it. They will walk about Westminster Abbey and knit, I feel sure. Meanwhile, Anne, we shall be living in Patty’s Place—and on Spofford Avenue. I feel like a millionairess even now.  <sub>[v3 c10 P36](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0036)</sub>

> Think of having a real live author at Patty’s Place  <sub>[v3 c36 P8](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0008)</sub>
